comments: Jordan, wanna take a look at this failure? @lkts can help with debugging.

Seems the issue is as follows:
1. The field "Xi" is configured with `dynamic: runtime`
2. The field "Xi.MPxl" is configured with `copy_to: oF.bf`
3. The field "oF.bf" is not explicitly mapped.
4. The DocumentParser incorrectly instantiates the "wrapper" DocumentParsingContext with the inherited value for `dynamic`.
5. Depending on which values the DocumentParser encounters first, different mappers are instantiated for "of.Bf"
    a. If the DocumentParser encounters a value for "oF.bf" first, then it will instantiate the default text mapper with a keyword multi-field.
    b. If the DocumentParser encounters a value for "Xi.MPxl" first, then the copy_to logic will run with the inherited `dynamic: runtime` and will instantiate a "no-op" field mapper for "oF.bf".
6. Documents are not necessarily reindexed in the same order in which they were originally indexed.

So when documents were initially indexed, the first value encountered was for "Xi.MPxl", and so a no-op field mapper was instantiated. But when documents were later reindexed, the order had changed such that the first value encountered was for "oF.bf" and so a text/keyword mapper was instantiated. This discrepancy in mapppings caused the assertion failure.

This behavior stems from the fact that DocumentParser incorrectly uses the inherited `dynamic` value for copy_to, a known issue in #113049 and soon to be solved in #121109.

Below is a minimal yaml test that reproduces the issue:
```yaml
"Index same documents in different order":
  - do :
      indices.put_index_template:
        name: generic_logs_template
        body:
          index_patterns: foo-*
          template:
            mappings:
              properties:
                host.name:
                  type: keyword
                Xi:
                  dynamic: "runtime"
                  properties:
                    MPxl:
                      type: "keyword"
                      copy_to: "oF.bf"
                      index: false
                      store: true
                      doc_values: false

  - do:
      bulk:
        index: foo-bar
        refresh: true
        body:
          - '{ "create": {"_id": 0 } }'
          - '{"@timestamp": "2024-01-01T10:00:00.000Z", "Xi": {"MPxl": "gqpPCJwZCyiTLjVrwVZhJfcYCHHdNVWRxcwTfcJNcGehYhSHvo"}, "oF": []}'
          - '{ "create": {"_id": 1 } }'
          - '{"@timestamp": "2024-01-01T10:00:01.000Z", "Xi": {"MPxl": "eczmLvJtOPeJMRmbfXIkwwNHgJAuqjfDERdkvluQ"}, "oF": []}'
          - '{ "create": {"_id": 2 } }'
          - '{"@timestamp": "2024-01-01T10:00:02.000Z", "Xi": [], "oF": [{"bf": ["YaUBqLB", "QZO"]}]}'
          - '{ "create": {"_id": 3 } }'
          - '{"@timestamp": "2024-01-01T10:00:03.000Z", "Xi": {"MPxl": []}, "oF": [{"bf": []}]}'

  - do:
      bulk:
        index: foo-baz
        refresh: true
        body:
          - '{ "create": {"_id": 2 } }'
          - '{"@timestamp": "2024-01-01T10:00:02.000Z", "Xi": [], "oF": [{"bf": ["YaUBqLB", "QZO"]}]}'
          - '{ "create": {"_id": 3 } }'
          - '{"@timestamp": "2024-01-01T10:00:03.000Z", "Xi": {"MPxl": []}, "oF": [{"bf": []}]}'
          - '{ "create": {"_id": 0 } }'
          - '{"@timestamp": "2024-01-01T10:00:00.000Z", "Xi": {"MPxl": "gqpPCJwZCyiTLjVrwVZhJfcYCHHdNVWRxcwTfcJNcGehYhSHvo"}, "oF": []}'
          - '{ "create": {"_id": 1 } }'
          - '{"@timestamp": "2024-01-01T10:00:01.000Z", "Xi": {"MPxl": "eczmLvJtOPeJMRmbfXIkwwNHgJAuqjfDERdkvluQ"}, "oF": []}'

  - do:
      indices.get_mapping:
        index: foo-bar
  - set: { foo-bar: mappings_baseline}

  - do:
      indices.get_mapping:
        index: foo-baz
  - match:
      foo-baz: $mappings_baseline

  - do:
      field_caps:
        index: foo-bar
        fields: "*"
  - set: { fields: fieldcaps_baseline }

  - do:
      field_caps:
        index: foo-baz
        fields: "*"
  - match:
      fields: $fieldcaps_baseline

```
Nice, good investigation Jordan! Debugging these tests is very tricky, well done.

review_comments: Note that the call site didn't change here, this works because `createCopyToContext` is the only place that passes a root maper to `Wrapper` constructor. I think this is fragile but i don't have anything better.
Shall we create a factory method like `createWithRootDynamic` and use it explicitly?
It's an optioin but you still need this constructor to call `super`.
